test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2021: Official Paper (Held On : 6 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In an election that was contested by 2 candidates, one candidate got 20% of the total votes and yet lost by 600 votes. What is the total number of votes cast in the election assuming all votes are valid?
solution:
Given:

Percentage of votes got by losing candidates = 20%

Number of votes by which losing candidate lost = 600 votes

Concept used:

Total number of votes = Number of votes secured by A + Number of votes secured by B

Calculation:

Let the total number of votes be x.

Number of votes losing candidate got = x × (20/100)

⇒ 0.20x

Number of votes winning candidate got = 0.20x + 600

Then, Total number of votes = 0.20x + 0.20x + 600 = x

⇒ 0.40x + 600 = x

⇒ x – 0.40x = 600

⇒ 0.60x = 600

⇒ x = 1000

∴ The total number of votes is 1000.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Let the total vote be 100%.

The winner received 80% of the total votes. 

The Loser received 20% of the total votes. 

Difference = 80% - 20% = 60%

Value of 60% ≡ 600

⇒ 100% ≡ 1000

∴ The total number of votes is 1000.
